prompt:
An on-demand instance costs $0.192/hour. A 1-year partial-upfront Reserved Instance costs $1000 upfront plus $0.075/hour. Assuming the instance runs 730 hours per month, after how many months (fractional, 2 decimals) does the RI become cheaper than on-demand (break-even point)?

(No data files are needed for this task; you may still use Python for the arithmetic.)

Required final answer format (JSON inside <answer></answer> tags):
{"months": <number>}

tool_calls.name: run_python
tool_calls.code:
# On-demand: 0.192/hour
# RI: 1000 upfront + 0.075/hour
# Hours per month: 730

od_monthly = 0.192 * 730
ri_monthly_run = 0.075 * 730

# Break-even: 1000 + ri_monthly_run * m = od_monthly * m
m = 1000 / (od_monthly - ri_monthly_run)
print(od_monthly, ri_monthly_run, m, round(m, 2))
